content: The recommendations aim to guide the prioritization of new and existing questions for the development and updating of guidelines by the World Health Organization (WHO). These recommendations will be reviewed and prioritized by the Executive Guideline Steering Group (GSG). If new evidence emerges that could significantly impact the current evidence base, the recommendations may be updated. In the absence of new reports or information, the recommendations may be revalidated. After the publication and dissemination of updated recommendations, any concerns regarding their validity will be promptly communicated to guideline implementers, along with plans for further updates if necessary. WHO also encourages suggestions for additional questions to be included in the updated recommendations. The WHO recommendations address the policy of interventionist versus expectant management of severe pre-eclampsia before term. This includes a systematic review of evidence, such as maternal and fetal outcomes, to determine the most effective approach. Maternal outcomes include pre-eclampsia, eclampsia, recurrent seizures, ICU admission, severe maternal morbidity, maternal death, and adverse effects of interventions. Fetal and neonatal outcomes include Apgar scores, NICU admissions, and perinatal deaths. The evidence on the effects of interventionist care versus expectant management for severe pre-eclampsia between 24 and 34 weeks of gestation is derived from a Cochrane systematic review, which includes six trials involving 748 women. The review evaluates the impact of immediate delivery (via cesarean section or induction) compared to expectant management or no treatment on maternal and fetal outcomes.
